evidence: Plin. NH 9.42: nūllum animal graviōre somnō premitur
terms.comment: “No” before a noun. “And no” is nec ūllus (see any); with persons, “no one” is nēmō; “no …” of a quantity is often nihil with a genitive (below).

terms.gloss: no (amount of): no news, no warmth
terms.grammar: indeclinable pronoun with a partitive genitive
terms.comment: For “no” before a mass or abstract noun: nihil novī, no news; nihil calōris, no warmth (see nothing).

phrases.english: no oil came out of it

phrases.latin: sī rem nūllam habēbis, quod in buccam vēnerit scrībitō
phrases.english: if you have no news, write whatever comes into your mouth

phrases.latin: sōl fervit, et fit nihil; it diēs, et amīcī nūllī eunt
phrases.english: the sun blazes and nothing happens; the day goes by, and no friends come

phrases.latin: nōn captō ante cibō, nōn ope ūllā ad arcendum frīgus adhibitā, nihil calōris inerat
phrases.english: they had eaten nothing beforehand and had nothing to keep out the cold, so there was no warmth in them

sources: Lewis & Short: nullus · Lewis & Short: nihil
